title: CTS Unit 6 — The Rise of Pentecostalism, 1901–1910s / El surgimiento del pentecostalismo, 1901–1910

blocks.en: Pentecostalism & the Charismatic Movement · Unit 6
blocks.es_reference: El pentecostalismo y el movimiento carismático · Unidad 6

blocks.en: The Rise of Pentecostalism, 1901–1910s
blocks.es_reference: El surgimiento del pentecostalismo, 1901–década de 1910

blocks.en: A Biblical Study · New King James Version
blocks.es_reference: Un estudio bíblico · Reina-Valera Gómez

blocks.en: "But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me… to the end of the earth."Acts 1:8 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Pero recibiréis poder, cuando haya venido sobre vosotros el Espíritu Santo, y me seréis testigos… hasta lo último de la tierra."Hechos 1:8 (RVG)

blocks.en: Learning Objectives
blocks.es_reference: Objetivos de aprendizaje

blocks.en: Explain why modern Pentecostalism, unlike most traditions, can be dated to a specific time and place, and name the nineteenth-century roots it grew from.
blocks.es_reference: Explicar por qué el pentecostalismo moderno, a diferencia de la mayoría de las tradiciones, puede fecharse en un tiempo y lugar específicos, y nombrar las raíces del siglo diecinueve de las que creció.

blocks.en: Recount the events at Topeka in 1901 and the rise of Parham's doctrine of tongues as initial evidence.
blocks.es_reference: Relatar los eventos en Topeka en 1901 y el surgimiento de la doctrina de Parham de las lenguas como evidencia inicial.

blocks.en: Trace the Azusa Street revival under William Seymour and its spread into a worldwide movement.
blocks.es_reference: Trazar el avivamiento de la Calle Azusa bajo William Seymour y su expansión en un movimiento mundial.

blocks.en: Describe the interracial character of Azusa Street and honestly assess the resistance and division that followed.
blocks.es_reference: Describir el carácter interracial de la Calle Azusa y evaluar con honestidad la resistencia y la división que siguieron.

blocks.en: Tell the movement's origin fairly — honoring the fruit, naming human failure, and locating the doctrinal assessment in other units.
blocks.es_reference: Contar el origen del movimiento con justicia — honrando el fruto, nombrando el fracaso humano, y ubicando la evaluación doctrinal en otras unidades.

blocks.en: A Movement with a Birthday
blocks.es_reference: Un movimiento con fecha de nacimiento

blocks.en: Most Christian traditions trace their beginnings back across many centuries, their origins lost in the slow growth of the church. Modern Pentecostalism is different. It can be dated, with unusual precision, to the first years of the twentieth century — to a Bible school in Topeka, Kansas, in 1901, and above all to a humble mission on Azusa Street in Los Angeles beginning in 1906. Within a single generation, what started among a handful of praying students had become a worldwide movement. This unit tells that story: the soil it grew in, the people God used, and the teaching that came to mark it.
blocks.es_reference: La mayoría de las tradiciones cristianas rastrean sus comienzos a través de muchos siglos, con sus orígenes perdidos en el lento crecimiento de la iglesia. El pentecostalismo moderno es diferente. Puede fecharse, con precisión inusual, en los primeros años del siglo veinte — en una escuela bíblica en Topeka, Kansas, en 1901, y sobre todo en una humilde misión en la Calle Azusa en Los Ángeles a partir de 1906. En una sola generación, lo que comenzó entre un puñado de estudiantes que oraban se había convertido en un movimiento mundial. Esta unidad cuenta esa historia: el terreno en que creció, las personas que Dios usó, y la enseñanza que llegó a marcarlo.

blocks.en: We tell it as history. Our task here is to describe what happened and what was taught fairly and accurately, giving thanks for the good and being honest about the failures, while reserving the weighing of doctrine for the units that take it up directly. In particular, the question of tongues as the evidence of the Spirit's baptism — the doctrine born in these very years — is examined elsewhere in this course; here we simply record its origin. Throughout, we keep the two questions of this course apart: whether a gift is real is one matter, and whether a particular experience is required of every believer is another.
blocks.es_reference: La contamos como historia. Nuestra tarea aquí es describir lo que sucedió y lo que se enseñó con justicia y exactitud, dando gracias por lo bueno y siendo honestos sobre los fracasos, mientras reservamos el sopesar la doctrina para las unidades que la tratan directamente. En particular, la cuestión de las lenguas como evidencia del bautismo del Espíritu — la doctrina nacida en estos mismos años — se examina en otras partes de este curso; aquí simplemente registramos su origen. A lo largo de todo, mantenemos separadas las dos preguntas de este curso: si un don es real es un asunto, y si una experiencia particular se requiere de todo creyente es otro.

blocks.en: The Soil It Grew In
blocks.es_reference: El terreno en que creció

blocks.en: Pentecostalism did not appear out of nothing. It grew from soil that had been prepared through the whole of the nineteenth century. The Holiness movement, drawing on John Wesley's teaching, had taught believers to seek a definite second work of grace — an experience of entire sanctification beyond conversion. The Keswick or higher-life movement pressed a similar hunger for a deeper, Spirit-filled Christian life. Movements of divine healing spread the expectation that God still worked wonders among His people, and that His power was not shut up in the past.
blocks.es_reference: El pentecostalismo no apareció de la nada. Creció de un terreno que había sido preparado a lo largo de todo el siglo diecinueve. El movimiento de santidad, apoyándose en la enseñanza de Juan Wesley, había enseñado a los creyentes a buscar una segunda obra de gracia definida — una experiencia de entera santificación más allá de la conversión. El movimiento de Keswick o de la vida superior urgía un anhelo semejante de una vida cristiana más profunda y llena del Espíritu. Los movimientos de sanidad divina extendían la expectativa de que Dios todavía obraba maravillas entre su pueblo, y que su poder no estaba encerrado en el pasado.

blocks.en: "And it shall come to pass afterward that I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy…"Joel 2:28 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Y será que después de esto, derramaré mi Espíritu sobre toda carne, y profetizarán vuestros hijos y vuestras hijas…"Joel 2:28 (RVG)

blocks.en: Above all, many earnest Christians had come to expect a great outpouring of the Spirit before the return of Christ — a latter rain, they called it, reading the promise of Joel and its fulfillment at Pentecost as a pattern God would renew in the last days. Prayer meetings across America and beyond were pleading for such a visitation. So when it seemed to come, it fell on ground already plowed and watered by decades of longing.
blocks.es_reference: Sobre todo, muchos cristianos sinceros habían llegado a esperar un gran derramamiento del Espíritu antes del regreso de Cristo — una lluvia tardía, la llamaban, leyendo la promesa de Joel y su cumplimiento en Pentecostés como un patrón que Dios renovaría en los postreros días. Reuniones de oración por toda América y más allá suplicaban tal visitación. Así que cuando pareció llegar, cayó sobre un terreno ya arado y regado por décadas de anhelo.

blocks.en: The expectancy only intensified as the new century opened: news of a mighty revival in Wales in 1904 and 1905, under the young preacher Evan Roberts, swept through the churches and convinced many that God was again visiting His people. To hearts already watching for a latter rain, such reports were kindling.
blocks.es_reference: La expectación solo se intensificó al abrirse el nuevo siglo: las noticias de un poderoso avivamiento en Gales en 1904 y 1905, bajo el joven predicador Evan Roberts, recorrieron las iglesias y convencieron a muchos de que Dios visitaba de nuevo a su pueblo. Para corazones que ya velaban esperando una lluvia tardía, tales informes eran leña para el fuego.

blocks.en: Topeka and the First Outpouring, 1901
blocks.es_reference: Topeka y el primer derramamiento, 1901

blocks.en: Charles Fox Parham was a Holiness preacher and teacher who, at the close of 1900, opened Bethel Bible School in Topeka, Kansas. He set his students a question: what does the Bible give as the evidence that a person has received the baptism in the Holy Spirit? As they searched the book of Acts, they concluded that the sign, again and again, was speaking in tongues.
blocks.es_reference: Charles Fox Parham era un predicador y maestro de santidad que, al cierre de 1900, abrió la Escuela Bíblica Betel en Topeka, Kansas. Planteó a sus estudiantes una pregunta: ¿qué da la Biblia como la evidencia de que una persona ha recibido el bautismo en el Espíritu Santo? Al escudriñar el libro de los Hechos, concluyeron que la señal, una y otra vez, era el hablar en lenguas.

blocks.en: "And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance."Acts 2:4 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Y fueron todos llenos del Espíritu Santo, y comenzaron a hablar en otras lenguas, según el Espíritu les daba que hablasen."Hechos 2:4 (RVG)

blocks.en: On the first day of January 1901, a student named Agnes Ozman asked Parham to lay hands on her that she might receive the Spirit, and she began to speak in what those present took to be a foreign language. In the days that followed, others in the school had the same experience, and Parham himself among them. From this beginning he drew the teaching that would define the movement he was helping to birth.
blocks.es_reference: En el primer día de enero de 1901, una estudiante llamada Agnes Ozman pidió a Parham que le impusiera las manos para recibir el Espíritu, y comenzó a hablar en lo que los presentes tomaron por una lengua extranjera. En los días siguientes, otros en la escuela tuvieron la misma experiencia, y Parham mismo entre ellos. De este comienzo sacó la enseñanza que definiría el movimiento que estaba ayudando a dar a luz.

blocks.en: Parham's Doctrine of "Initial Evidence"
blocks.es_reference: La doctrina de Parham de la "evidencia inicial"

blocks.en: Parham taught that speaking in tongues is the uniform initial evidence of the baptism in the Holy Spirit — that whenever a believer is so baptized, tongues will follow as the Bible sign. At first he and his followers believed these tongues were real, known foreign languages, given by God to equip missionaries to preach the gospel in lands whose speech they had never learned. This hope of "missionary tongues" faded when those who went abroad found they still had to learn the local languages in the ordinary way; but the core doctrine — tongues as the required evidence of Spirit-baptism — remained, and became the hallmark of early Pentecostalism.
blocks.es_reference: Parham enseñó que el hablar en lenguas es la evidencia inicial uniforme del bautismo en el Espíritu Santo — que siempre que un creyente es así bautizado, las lenguas seguirán como la señal bíblica. Al principio él y sus seguidores creían que estas lenguas eran idiomas extranjeros reales y conocidos, dados por Dios para equipar a los misioneros a predicar el evangelio en tierras cuya habla nunca habían aprendido. Esta esperanza de "lenguas misioneras" se desvaneció cuando los que fueron al extranjero hallaron que aún tenían que aprender los idiomas locales de la manera ordinaria; pero la doctrina central — las lenguas como la evidencia requerida del bautismo del Espíritu — permaneció, y llegó a ser el sello del pentecostalismo temprano.

blocks.en: Their reasoning ran from the pattern they saw in the book of Acts. There the Spirit's coming was accompanied by tongues at Pentecost, again at the house of Cornelius, and again at Ephesus; from these accounts they inferred that tongues was the God-appointed sign for every believer who received the baptism. Whether that inference holds — whether a repeated occurrence amounts to a universal rule — is exactly the question the course examines in its units on Acts and on Spirit-baptism, and it need not be settled here.
blocks.es_reference: Su razonamiento corría desde el patrón que veían en el libro de los Hechos. Allí la venida del Espíritu fue acompañada de lenguas en Pentecostés, otra vez en la casa de Cornelio, y otra vez en Éfeso; de estos relatos infirieron que las lenguas eran la señal designada por Dios para todo creyente que recibía el bautismo. Si esa inferencia se sostiene — si una ocurrencia repetida equivale a una regla universal — es exactamente la pregunta que el curso examina en sus unidades sobre Hechos y sobre el bautismo del Espíritu, y no necesita resolverse aquí.

blocks.en: It is this teaching, more than any other, that has distinguished the movement from the wider church. The present course takes it up directly in the units on tongues in Acts, on the baptism in the Spirit, and in the closing assessment, where it is weighed by Scripture and, as a universal rule for every believer, respectfully declined. Here we neither argue nor settle it; we simply record that at Topeka, in the first days of a new century, the doctrine was born. And we keep the distinction the course has insisted upon throughout: to question whether tongues must accompany every Spirit-baptism is not to deny that the gift of tongues is real.
blocks.es_reference: Es esta enseñanza, más que ninguna otra, la que ha distinguido al movimiento de la iglesia más amplia. El presente curso la trata directamente en las unidades sobre las lenguas en Hechos, sobre el bautismo en el Espíritu, y en la evaluación final, donde se sopesa por la Escritura y, como regla universal para todo creyente, se declina respetuosamente. Aquí ni la argumentamos ni la resolvemos; simplemente registramos que en Topeka, en los primeros días de un nuevo siglo, la doctrina nació. Y mantenemos la distinción que el curso ha insistido a lo largo de todo: cuestionar si las lenguas deben acompañar todo bautismo del Espíritu no es negar que el don de lenguas sea real.

blocks.en: Houston, and a Student Named Seymour
blocks.es_reference: Houston, y un estudiante llamado Seymour

blocks.en: Parham soon moved his work to Texas, and around 1905 opened a Bible school in Houston. Among those drawn to learn from him was William J. Seymour, a Black Holiness preacher, the son of former slaves, marked by a deep and humble piety. Under the segregation laws of that time and place, Seymour was not allowed to sit in the classroom with the white students; he listened to Parham's lectures from the hallway, through a door left ajar. Whatever indignity this involved, Seymour received the message that a baptism in the Spirit, evidenced by tongues, was offered to the church in his own day — and he would carry it further than his teacher ever did.
blocks.es_reference: Parham pronto trasladó su obra a Texas, y alrededor de 1905 abrió una escuela bíblica en Houston. Entre los atraídos a aprender de él estaba William J. Seymour, un predicador negro de santidad, hijo de antiguos esclavos, marcado por una piedad profunda y humilde. Bajo las leyes de segregación de aquel tiempo y lugar, a Seymour no se le permitía sentarse en el aula con los estudiantes blancos; escuchaba las lecciones de Parham desde el pasillo, por una puerta dejada entreabierta. Cualquiera que fuese la indignidad que esto implicaba, Seymour recibió el mensaje de que un bautismo en el Espíritu, evidenciado por lenguas, se ofrecía a la iglesia en su propio día — y lo llevaría más lejos de lo que su maestro jamás lo hizo.

blocks.en: Azusa Street, 1906
blocks.es_reference: La Calle Azusa, 1906

blocks.en: Invited to preach at a small Holiness congregation in Los Angeles, Seymour proclaimed that the baptism in the Spirit with the sign of tongues was for the present hour. The reception was mixed; he was for a time locked out of the very church that had called him. He began instead to hold meetings in a private home on Bonnie Brae Street, and there, in April of 1906, the outpouring he had preached about came upon the little gathering. Days later, on the eighteenth of April, the great San Francisco earthquake shook California, and to many the timing seemed a sign that God was doing something momentous; the crowds only grew. The house could not hold them — its front porch is said to have collapsed under the press of people — and the work moved to a plain, abandoned building at 312 Azusa Street.
blocks.es_reference: Invitado a predicar en una pequeña congregación de santidad en Los Ángeles, Seymour proclamó que el bautismo en el Espíritu con la señal de lenguas era para la hora presente. La recepción fue mixta; por un tiempo quedó excluido de la misma iglesia que lo había llamado. Comenzó en cambio a tener reuniones en una casa particular en la Calle Bonnie Brae, y allí, en abril de 1906, el derramamiento que había predicado vino sobre la pequeña reunión. Días después, el dieciocho de abril, el gran terremoto de San Francisco sacudió California, y a muchos el momento les pareció una señal de que Dios estaba haciendo algo trascendental; las multitudes solo crecieron. La casa no podía contenerlas — se dice que su porche delantero se derrumbó bajo la presión de la gente — y la obra se trasladó a un edificio sencillo y abandonado en el número 312 de la Calle Azusa.

blocks.en: "There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus."Galatians 3:28 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "No hay judío ni griego; no hay siervo ni libre; no hay varón ni mujer; porque todos vosotros sois uno en Cristo Jesús."Gálatas 3:28 (RVG)

blocks.en: There, for about three years, services ran morning, afternoon, and night, drawing the curious and the hungry from across the city and, before long, from around the world. What amazed observers as much as the tongues and the reported healings was something else entirely: Black and white, rich and poor, immigrant and native-born, men and women, worshiping and praying side by side as equals — and this in an age of rigid, legally enforced segregation. One who was there wrote that at Azusa the color line was washed away in the blood of Christ. From that mission a little newspaper, The Apostolic Faith, was sent out freely and was soon reaching tens of thousands of readers across the nation and over the seas.
blocks.es_reference: Allí, por unos tres años, los cultos corrían mañana, tarde y noche, atrayendo a los curiosos y a los hambrientos de toda la ciudad y, en poco tiempo, de todo el mundo. Lo que asombró a los observadores tanto como las lenguas y las sanidades reportadas fue algo enteramente distinto: negros y blancos, ricos y pobres, inmigrantes y nativos, hombres y mujeres, adorando y orando lado a lado como iguales — y esto en una época de segregación rígida y legalmente impuesta. Uno que estuvo allí escribió que en Azusa la línea del color fue lavada en la sangre de Cristo. De aquella misión un pequeño periódico, The Apostolic Faith, se enviaba gratuitamente y pronto llegaba a decenas de miles de lectores por toda la nación y allende los mares.

blocks.en: The Message Goes Worldwide
blocks.es_reference: El mensaje va por todo el mundo

blocks.en: The spread was astonishingly swift. Visitors to Azusa returned home aflame; men and women sailed as missionaries with the message; and within a few short years Pentecostal works had sprung up across North America, Europe, Latin America, Africa, and Asia. New fellowships were formed to give the growing movement teaching and order — among them the Church of God in Christ, under C. H. Mason, who visited Azusa in 1907, and, in 1914, the Assemblies of God. What had begun with a handful of students praying in a Kansas schoolhouse had become, within a single generation, one of the great missionary movements in the history of the church — the seed of the hundreds of millions who would name the name of Christ in this tradition a century later.
blocks.es_reference: La expansión fue asombrosamente veloz. Los visitantes de Azusa volvían a casa encendidos; hombres y mujeres zarparon como misioneros con el mensaje; y en pocos años obras pentecostales habían surgido por toda Norteamérica, Europa, América Latina, África y Asia. Nuevas hermandades se formaron para dar enseñanza y orden al movimiento creciente — entre ellas la Iglesia de Dios en Cristo, bajo C. H. Mason, quien visitó Azusa en 1907, y, en 1914, las Asambleas de Dios. Lo que había comenzado con un puñado de estudiantes orando en una escuela de Kansas se había convertido, en una sola generación, en uno de los grandes movimientos misioneros en la historia de la iglesia — la semilla de los cientos de millones que invocarían el nombre de Cristo en esta tradición un siglo después.

blocks.en: The reach was truly global. The message crossed to Europe, where a Norwegian pastor, T. B. Barratt, became an early channel to the continent; it took root in Chile and Brazil, in parts of Africa, and in India, where a parallel outpouring had already stirred the Mukti Mission under Pandita Ramabai. Within a decade Pentecostal congregations could be found on every inhabited continent, often among the poor and the overlooked, and often carried by unschooled believers who simply went and told what they had seen.
blocks.es_reference: El alcance fue verdaderamente global. El mensaje cruzó a Europa, donde un pastor noruego, T. B. Barratt, llegó a ser un canal temprano al continente; echó raíces en Chile y Brasil, en partes de África, y en la India, donde un derramamiento paralelo ya había conmovido la Misión Mukti bajo Pandita Ramabai. En una década podían hallarse congregaciones pentecostales en todos los continentes habitados, a menudo entre los pobres y los olvidados, y a menudo llevadas por creyentes sin instrucción que simplemente iban y contaban lo que habían visto.

blocks.en: Reading the History Fairly
blocks.es_reference: Leyendo la historia con justicia

blocks.en: An honest account does not tidy away the difficulties, and there were real ones. Charles Parham, the man who first framed the doctrine, saw his own influence wane within a few years amid controversy, and his later life was clouded; it was the humble mission at Azusa Street, under Seymour, that proved to be the movement's more enduring fountainhead. The very interracial worship that so marked Azusa met resistance from some early leaders — Parham among them — who could not accept it.
blocks.es_reference: Un relato honesto no esconde las dificultades, y las hubo reales. Charles Parham, el hombre que primero formuló la doctrina, vio su propia influencia menguar en pocos años en medio de controversia, y su vida posterior quedó nublada; fue la humilde misión en la Calle Azusa, bajo Seymour, la que resultó ser la fuente más perdurable del movimiento. La misma adoración interracial que tanto marcó a Azusa encontró resistencia de algunos líderes tempranos — Parham entre ellos — que no podían aceptarla.

blocks.en: More sorrowful still, many of the fellowships that formed in the following years divided along the very color line the revival had, for a season, erased, so that a movement born in a remarkable unity too often settled back into the divisions of its age. We record all this not to diminish what God did but to tell the truth: a genuine work of the Spirit still passes through weak, sinful, and shortsighted people. As always in this course, we judge the movement by Scripture and by its faithful, not by its failures or its worst moments — and we give thanks for the grace that worked through such ordinary vessels.
blocks.es_reference: Más triste aún, muchas de las hermandades que se formaron en los años siguientes se dividieron por la misma línea del color que el avivamiento había, por una temporada, borrado, de modo que un movimiento nacido en una notable unidad demasiado a menudo volvió a asentarse en las divisiones de su época. Registramos todo esto no para disminuir lo que Dios hizo, sino para decir la verdad: una obra genuina del Espíritu todavía pasa por personas débiles, pecadoras y de corta vista. Como siempre en este curso, juzgamos el movimiento por la Escritura y por sus fieles, no por sus fracasos ni por sus peores momentos — y damos gracias por la gracia que obró a través de vasijas tan ordinarias.

blocks.en: It is worth adding that historians often note how Pentecostal-like outpourings appeared in several places at nearly the same time — Topeka, Wales, the Mukti Mission in India, and then Azusa — which has led many to see the movement less as the invention of a single teacher than as a broad stirring across one era. However one weighs that question, it guards us against pinning either the credit or the blame on one man, and it points us, as Scripture does, to the God who pours out His Spirit where and as He wills.
blocks.es_reference: Vale la pena añadir que los historiadores a menudo notan cómo derramamientos semejantes al pentecostal aparecieron en varios lugares casi al mismo tiempo — Topeka, Gales, la Misión Mukti en la India, y luego Azusa — lo cual ha llevado a muchos a ver el movimiento menos como la invención de un solo maestro que como un amplio mover a través de una misma época. Cualquiera que sea la manera en que se sopese esa pregunta, nos guarda de atribuir el crédito o la culpa a un solo hombre, y nos señala, como lo hace la Escritura, al Dios que derrama su Espíritu donde y como quiere.

blocks.en: What the Story Teaches
blocks.es_reference: Lo que enseña la historia

blocks.en: The birth of Pentecostalism carries lessons for every Christian, whatever he concludes about its distinctive doctrine. It reminds us that God still visits His church, that a longing for His presence and power is not to be despised, and that the gospel of Christ has strength to cross the very lines that most divide people. It reminds us, too, that fervor must be wedded to sound doctrine and humble accountability, lest zeal run ahead of the Word and stumble. The questions first pressed at Topeka and Azusa we weigh carefully elsewhere; here it is enough to give thanks that, as a new century opened, God poured out His Spirit afresh and sent the good news of His Son toward the ends of the earth.
blocks.es_reference: El nacimiento del pentecostalismo lleva lecciones para todo cristiano, cualquiera que sea su conclusión sobre su doctrina distintiva. Nos recuerda que Dios todavía visita a su iglesia, que un anhelo de su presencia y poder no ha de despreciarse, y que el evangelio de Cristo tiene fuerza para cruzar las mismas líneas que más dividen a las personas. Nos recuerda, también, que el fervor debe unirse a la sana doctrina y a la humilde rendición de cuentas, no sea que el celo corra delante de la Palabra y tropiece. Las preguntas planteadas primero en Topeka y Azusa las sopesamos con cuidado en otras partes; aquí basta con dar gracias de que, al abrirse un nuevo siglo, Dios derramó su Espíritu de nuevo y envió las buenas nuevas de su Hijo hacia los confines de la tierra.

blocks.en: Looking Ahead
blocks.es_reference: Mirando adelante

blocks.en: In the next unit we follow the story forward to the middle and later twentieth century, when the Pentecostal experience spilled beyond its own new denominations and into the historic churches — the Charismatic Renewal and the movements that came to be called the Third Wave.
blocks.es_reference: En la próxima unidad seguimos la historia hacia adelante, al siglo veinte medio y tardío, cuando la experiencia pentecostal se desbordó más allá de sus propias nuevas denominaciones y entró en las iglesias históricas — la Renovación Carismática y los movimientos que llegaron a llamarse la Tercera Ola.

blocks.en: Discussion Questions
blocks.es_reference: Preguntas para discusión

blocks.en: Why is it significant that a hunger for a fresh outpouring of the Spirit had been building for decades before 1901?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Por qué es significativo que un hambre de un derramamiento fresco del Espíritu se había estado acumulando por décadas antes de 1901?

blocks.en: What was Parham's doctrine of initial evidence, and why does this course examine it elsewhere rather than settle it here?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Cuál era la doctrina de Parham de la evidencia inicial, y por qué este curso la examina en otras partes en vez de resolverla aquí?

blocks.en: What made the interracial worship at Azusa Street remarkable, and what does the later division teach us about revival passing through sinful people?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Qué hizo notable la adoración interracial en la Calle Azusa, y qué nos enseña la división posterior sobre el avivamiento que pasa por personas pecadoras?

blocks.en: How can we hold together gratitude for a genuine work of God and honesty about the failures of those involved in it?

mc.stem: Modern Pentecostalism is unusual among Christian traditions in that —
options: it has no connection to any earlier movement
it rejects the Bible
it can be traced to a specific time and place in the early twentieth century
it began in the first century and never changed
mc.why: Its modern rise is datable to Topeka (1901) and Azusa Street (1906), though it grew from older Holiness and higher-life roots.

mc.stem: The nineteenth-century soil from which Pentecostalism grew included —
options: the prosperity gospel
the Holiness movement, higher-life teaching, divine-healing movements, and expectation of a latter-rain outpouring
modern television ministry
the rejection of the Holy Spirit
mc.why: Many believers were already praying for a fresh outpouring, shaped by Wesleyan sanctification and “latter rain” expectation.

mc.stem: The event traditionally marked as the beginning was —
options: the Assemblies of God founding in 1914
the San Francisco earthquake
Parham's death
Agnes Ozman speaking in tongues at Topeka on January 1, 1901
mc.why: At Parham's Bethel Bible School, Ozman's experience gave rise to the doctrine that would define the movement.

mc.stem: Parham's doctrine of “initial evidence” taught that —
options: speaking in tongues is the uniform initial evidence of the baptism in the Holy Spirit
tongues are unimportant
only apostles could receive the Spirit
the Spirit is not a person
mc.why: Tongues as the required sign of Spirit-baptism became the movement's hallmark; the course weighs and, as a universal rule, respectfully declines it elsewhere.

mc.stem: William J. Seymour, who led the Azusa Street revival, first heard the message —
options: in Los Angeles as a child
from a book he had written
in Houston, listening to Parham's lectures from the hallway under the segregation of the day
in Africa
mc.why: Seymour, a Black Holiness preacher and son of former slaves, carried the message from Parham's Houston school to Los Angeles.

mc.stem: What struck observers about the Azusa Street meetings, alongside tongues and healings, was —
options: their great wealth
their use of television
their rejection of Scripture
Black and white, rich and poor, worshiping together as equals in an age of rigid segregation
mc.why: One participant wrote that the color line was “washed away in the blood” — a striking witness for its time, though resistance and later division followed.

mc.stem: This unit tells the movement's origin story —
options: as a flawless triumph with no failures
as history — describing fairly, honoring the fruit, and honestly naming human failure, while reserving doctrinal assessment for other units
in order to condemn the whole movement
without any reference to Scripture
mc.why: A fair account gives thanks for what God did, is honest about controversy and division, and weighs doctrine elsewhere by Scripture and the movement's faithful.

sa.prompt: Describe the nineteenth-century roots from which Pentecostalism grew.
sa.model: Pentecostalism did not appear from nowhere but grew from deep nineteenth-century roots. Chief among them was the Holiness movement, with its Wesleyan hunger for a second blessing of entire sanctification, and the related higher-life or Keswick teaching. Alongside these ran the divine-healing movements and a widespread expectation that God would send a latter-rain outpouring of the Spirit before Christ's return, reading Joel and Acts as promise. Many earnest believers were already praying for such a fresh outpouring, so the ground was well prepared when it came.

sa.prompt: Explain who Agnes Ozman, Charles Parham, and William Seymour were and their part in the movement's beginning.
sa.model: Charles Parham was the Holiness preacher whose Bible school in Topeka concluded that tongues was the evidence of Spirit-baptism, and who formulated the initial-evidence doctrine. Agnes Ozman was the student who, on the first day of 1901, spoke in tongues and became the traditional first instance under that teaching. William Seymour was a Black preacher who learned the message from Parham in Houston, listening from the hallway under segregation, and then carried it to Los Angeles, where he led the Azusa Street revival from which the movement spread across the world.

sa.prompt: How does this unit tell the history fairly, and where does it place the doctrinal assessment of what was taught?
sa.model: The unit tells the story as history, describing what happened and what was taught fairly rather than arguing the doctrine on the spot. It gives thanks for the fruit — a genuine visitation and a gospel that crossed the color line — while honestly naming human failure, including Parham's clouded later years and the sad division along racial lines that followed. It keeps two questions apart and places the doctrinal assessment of the initial-evidence teaching elsewhere in the course, where every claim is weighed by Scripture and the movement is judged by its faithful.

sa.prompt: What was the 'latter rain' expectation, and how did the Welsh revival intensify it?
sa.model: Many earnest Christians expected a great outpouring of the Spirit before the return of Christ, a latter rain, reading the promise of Joel and its fulfillment at Pentecost as a pattern God would renew in the last days, and prayer meetings across America and beyond pleaded for such a visitation. News of the revival in Wales in 1904 and 1905 under the young preacher Evan Roberts swept through the churches and convinced many that God was again visiting His people; to hearts already watching for a latter rain, such reports were kindling. So when the outpouring seemed to come, it fell on ground already plowed and watered by decades of longing.

sa.prompt: What question did Parham set his students at Topeka, and what happened on 1 January 1901?
sa.model: Charles Fox Parham, a Holiness preacher, opened Bethel Bible School in Topeka at the close of 1900 and set his students the question of what the Bible gives as the evidence that a person has received the baptism in the Holy Spirit; searching Acts, they concluded the sign was speaking in tongues. On the first day of January 1901 a student, Agnes Ozman, asked Parham to lay hands on her that she might receive the Spirit, and she began to speak in what those present took to be a foreign language; in the following days others, Parham among them, had the same experience.

sa.prompt: What were 'missionary tongues,' why did that hope fade, and what remained of Parham's doctrine?
sa.model: At first Parham and his followers believed the tongues were real, known foreign languages given by God to equip missionaries to preach in lands whose speech they had never learned. That hope faded when those who went abroad found they still had to learn the local languages in the ordinary way. But the core doctrine remained, that tongues is the uniform initial evidence of the baptism in the Holy Spirit, required whenever a believer is so baptized, and it became the hallmark of early Pentecostalism, reasoned from the pattern of Pentecost, Cornelius, and Ephesus.

sa.prompt: Who was William Seymour, and under what circumstances did he receive Parham's teaching in Houston?
sa.model: William J. Seymour was a Black Holiness preacher, the son of former slaves, marked by a deep and humble piety. Around 1905 Parham opened a Bible school in Houston, and under the segregation laws of that time and place Seymour was not allowed to sit in the classroom with the white students; he listened to the lectures from the hallway through a door left ajar. Whatever indignity this involved, he received the message that a baptism in the Spirit evidenced by tongues was offered to the church in his own day, and he would carry it further than his teacher ever did.

sa.prompt: Recount how the Azusa Street revival began, from Bonnie Brae Street to 312 Azusa Street.
sa.model: Invited to preach at a small Holiness congregation in Los Angeles, Seymour proclaimed the baptism in the Spirit with the sign of tongues for the present hour and was for a time locked out of the very church that had called him. He held meetings in a home on Bonnie Brae Street, where in April 1906 the outpouring came; days later the San Francisco earthquake seemed to many a sign, the crowds grew, the front porch is said to have collapsed under the press of people, and the work moved to an abandoned building at 312 Azusa Street. There for about three years services ran morning, afternoon, and night, and the paper The Apostolic Faith went out freely to tens of thousands.

sa.prompt: Describe the spread of the message from Azusa Street and name some of the fellowships and figures involved.
sa.model: Visitors returned home aflame, men and women sailed as missionaries, and within a few years Pentecostal works had sprung up across North America, Europe, Latin America, Africa, and Asia. New fellowships gave the movement teaching and order, among them the Church of God in Christ under C. H. Mason, who visited Azusa in 1907, and in 1914 the Assemblies of God. T. B. Barratt, a Norwegian pastor, became an early channel to Europe; the message took root in Chile and Brazil, in Africa, and in India, where a parallel outpouring had stirred the Mukti Mission under Pandita Ramabai. Within a decade there were congregations on every inhabited continent, often among the poor and carried by unschooled believers who simply went and told what they had seen.

sa.prompt: What lessons does the birth of Pentecostalism carry for every Christian, and why do historians hesitate to credit a single teacher?
sa.model: It reminds us that God still visits His church, that a longing for His presence and power is not to be despised, and that the gospel has strength to cross the lines that most divide people; and that fervor must be wedded to sound doctrine and humble accountability, lest zeal run ahead of the Word and stumble. Historians note that Pentecostal-like outpourings appeared in several places at nearly the same time, Topeka, Wales, the Mukti Mission in India, and then Azusa, which leads many to see the movement less as one teacher's invention than as a broad stirring across an era; that guards against pinning credit or blame on one man and points to the God who pours out His Spirit where and as He wills.
